# Styles

This file is the visual vocabulary: **what it looks like**. [`CRAFT.md`](./CRAFT.md)
is the technique arsenal: **how you render it**. They are separate on purpose, and
collapsing them is how runs end up templated.

The distinction is sharp because techniques are style-agnostic. `backdrop-filter`
builds the layered translucency of liquid glass, and it also builds the flat frosted
panels of a Swiss layout where the blur is the only softness on the page. A noise
shader is film grain in a cinematic grade and paper tooth in a risograph print. A
spring physics engine is playful in a claymorphic world and clinical in a blueprint.
The technique carries no opinion. The style is the opinion.

The order is fixed. **Style is chosen at Gate B1 with the concept**, from the brief,
the archetype, and the vision. **Techniques are assigned in Loop 2b to serve the
style that was already chosen.** Reaching for a style because you want to use a
shader is the tail wagging the dog, and it shows in the output.

Everything below is a starting position under `§3`. Read [the guardrails](#the-guardrails)
before you pick.

---

## Surface and material

**Glassmorphism.** Translucent panels floating over a substrate worth seeing through
to, legible because of the blur behind them rather than an opaque fill. Depth is
expressed as blur radius, the nearest layer blurring hardest and the farthest barely
at all, with a 1px semi-transparent light edge on each panel catching the implied
key light. Spacing runs generous because a panel needs background to be about.
**Implies** `backdrop-filter`, deliberate z-layering, `color-mix()` borders, a live
substrate. **Fails** as a stack of gray rectangles when the background is flat, and
fails `§12` the moment body copy sits on moving translucency. **Right when** depth is
the message and the background is itself content.

**Liquid glass.** Apple's 2025 material language, where the panel refracts rather
than merely blurs. Content behind the edge bends as it passes under, specular
highlights track a light source as the surface moves, and the whole shape lenses
during scroll so the page appears to be seen through a physical object. Real
implementation is an SDF or shader job with normals and a refraction pass;
`backdrop-filter` alone gets you glassmorphism with a name it did not earn.
**Implies** WebGL or a distortion shader, an SDF for the panel geometry, scroll-linked
light, a hard `§13` heavy-layer budget. **Fails** as expensive-looking chrome that
buries the work, breaking `§7`, and stutters on mid-range Android. **Right when** the
subject's work is material, tactile, or hardware, and the budget is declared.

**Neumorphism / soft UI.** Every element extruded from a single background hue by a
matched shadow pair, one dark and one light, cast from a consistent angle. There are
no borders and almost no color: form is entirely shadow, and the whole page sits in
one narrow tonal band. It fails contrast by default and only ships with the fix in
[Style and accessibility](#style-and-accessibility). **Implies** dual `box-shadow`,
one hue with lightness variation, a committed light direction. **Fails** as an
unreadable field of putty with invisible affordances. **Right when** exactly one
object is extruded and everything else is flat.

**Claymorphism.** Inflated, rounded volumes with large radii, soft ambient occlusion
at the base, and a bright saturated palette. Objects read as pressable toys with
thickness, lifted off the page by a diffuse colored shadow rather than a gray one.
Type sits heavy and rounded to match the geometry. **Implies** big `border-radius`,
layered colored shadows, spring motion on press, generous padding. **Fails** as
childish, which sinks a senior portfolio faster than anything else on this list.
**Right when** the subject's work is playful, consumer, or game-adjacent and the
copy can carry the seriousness.

**Skeuomorphic revival.** Real material simulation rather than nostalgic gloss:
paper with visible fiber, ink that bleeds into it, embossed metal with a directional
brush, edges worn where a thumb would rest. The rule is one material, simulated
honestly, with its physics respected everywhere. **Implies** generated textures under
`§10`, displacement or grain maps, per-material lighting, real shadow direction.
**Fails** as 2010 iOS pastiche the moment two materials appear on one surface without
a reason. **Right when** the subject's work has a physical antecedent and the
material can be named in one word.

**Aerogel / frosted depth.** Translucency without a light source, where layers are
milky and diffuse and depth reads as accumulated haze. Nothing has a hard edge;
separation comes from density, and the palette stays desaturated with light bleeding
between planes. **Implies** stacked low-opacity fills, large soft blurs, a fog
gradient, near-zero border weight. **Fails** as washed-out mush with no hierarchy
when every layer sits at the same density. **Right when** the subject's work is
atmospheric or scientific and hierarchy can be carried by type alone.

## Structural

**Swiss / International.** A visible modular grid, one type family at a strict scale,
flush-left ragged-right setting, and objective photography placed on grid intersections.
Whitespace is structural rather than decorative, and color is used once. Every
alignment is provable against the column. **Implies** CSS Grid with named lines, a
mathematical type scale, baseline rhythm, a single accent from `§8`. **Fails** as an
agency template, because it is the most-copied system in design and the grid alone
does not differentiate. **Right when** the work is dense and needs an authoritative
frame, and only with a collision or subversion applied.

**Brutalism.** Raw HTML honesty: system fonts, default link blue, visible borders,
unstyled form controls, structure exposed rather than hidden. The page looks like the
document it is, with layout that reveals the DOM rather than disguising it.
**Implies** near-zero CSS, system font stacks, native controls, no motion.
**Fails** as an excuse for laziness, indistinguishable from an unfinished build.
**Right when** the subject's credibility comes from substance and the refusal to
decorate is itself the position.

**Neo-brutalism.** Thick black borders, hard offset shadows with no blur, saturated
flat blocks of color, and heavy grotesque type at aggressive sizes. Elements sit at
slight rotations, overlapping without softening, and interaction moves the shadow
rather than fading anything. **Implies** solid `box-shadow` offsets, 2–4px borders,
transform on hover, a loud limited palette. **Fails** as Gumroad cosplay, since it is
currently the single most saturated style on the web. **Right when** the subject is
loud by nature and the collision partner supplies the restraint.

**Bento.** A dense grid of unequal cards, each self-contained, sized by importance
rather than content length. Radii are uniform, gaps are consistent, and the whole
composition reads as one object at a glance. **Implies** CSS Grid with spanning
areas, container queries, per-card art direction, a strict radius token.
**Fails** as a dashboard with nothing to show when the cards hold one metric each,
and hides narrative because every card is equal in reading order. **Right when** the
subject has many small things worth seeing simultaneously.

**Editorial / print.** Magazine mechanics carried honestly onto the screen: measured
columns, real hyphenation and justification, drop caps that sit on the baseline
grid, pull quotes breaking the measure, marginalia in the outer column, running
heads and folios. Type does all the work; images are placed as plates.
**Implies** `hyphens`, `text-wrap: pretty`, `initial-letter`, multi-column at
desktop only, a serif with real optical sizes, self-hosted per `§9`.
**Fails** when the measure runs past 75 characters or the columns force scroll-up
reading on mobile. **Right when** the case studies are long and the subject writes.

**Swiss-punk / Ray Gun.** The Swiss grid built and then deliberately violated: type
overlapping, rotated, set in conflicting families, letters cropped by the viewport,
lines running backwards. Type becomes image, legibility becomes a variable the
designer controls rather than a constant. **Implies** absolute positioning over a
grid, `mix-blend-mode`, variable-font extremes, cropped SVG text.
**Fails** as illegible noise when the underlying grid was never actually built, since
the violation only reads against visible order. **Right when** the subject is a
designer or musician and the audience reads visual sophistication.

## Atmospheric

**Cinematic dark.** A single key light with real falloff, deep vignette, film grain
sized to the viewport, and a graded palette where the blacks are lifted and tinted
rather than pure. Content sits in pools of light, and the space between them is
genuinely dark. **Implies** radial gradient key, grain shader or SVG turbulence, LUT
via `feColorMatrix` or a canvas pass, controlled bloom. **Fails** when the grade
crushes body copy below 4.5:1 and the grain eats small type. **Right when** the
work is visual and benefits from being lit rather than displayed.

**Aurora / mesh gradient.** Large soft color fields drifting across each other in
perceptual space, with no visible edges and no repeating pattern. Interpolation in
OKLCH keeps the midpoints saturated instead of going gray, and motion is slow enough
to be felt without being watched. **Implies** OKLCH gradients, canvas or WebGL mesh,
long-period animation, a grain overlay to defeat banding. **Fails** as the default AI
landing page, since it is the most generated look of the last three years.
**Right when** it is a substrate for another style rather than the style itself.

**Glow / neon.** A dark substrate with emissive accents that actually bloom, where
light spills past its source and tints what it lands on. Edges glow from the inside,
shadows take the accent hue, and the palette runs to two emissive colors at most.
**Implies** layered `box-shadow` bloom or a real bloom pass, dark tokens, hue-matched
shadows, restrained saturation on text. **Fails** as halation that makes every string
of text fringe and shimmer. **Right when** the work is nocturnal, musical, or
technical, and the emission points at the work.

**Vaporwave / Y2K.** Chromed type with environment reflection, gradient meshes in
cyan and magenta, CRT scanlines and phosphor bleed, grids receding to a horizon, and
deliberate JPEG and VHS artifacts. The nostalgia is specific to 1995–2003 hardware
and reads as a costume unless committed to fully. **Implies** SVG chrome gradients,
CRT shader, chromatic aberration, dithering, a period type pairing.
**Fails** as kitsch that dates the subject rather than the aesthetic.
**Right when** the audience shares the reference and the work is culture-adjacent.

**Solarpunk.** Organic growth forms and botanical geometry over warm optimistic
light: curves derived from phyllotaxis rather than arbitrary blobs, terracotta and
sage and brass, and layouts that branch rather than stack. Materials read as living
and sunlit, with growth used as the transition metaphor. **Implies** generative SVG
growth, warm gradients, curved layout paths, organic easing.
**Fails** as generic eco-branding with a leaf icon and a green button.
**Right when** the subject's work is climate, agriculture, health, or civic.

## Motion-native

These four are styles where the behavior **is** the aesthetic. A still screenshot
cannot represent them, which makes the `§12` reduced-motion design a first-class
deliverable rather than an afterthought.

**Kinetic.** Nothing is at rest. Type is in perpetual motion, marquees run at
different rates by depth, letters respond to pointer velocity, and the composition
recomposes continuously. Stillness is used once, as punctuation.
**Implies** scroll-velocity input, variable-font axis animation, `requestAnimationFrame`
loops, transform-only compositing. **Fails** as exhausting, and as unreadable when the
thing in motion is the thing being read. **Right when** the subject's work is
performance, motion, or sound.

**Physics-world.** Spring, inertia, mass, and collision are the interaction model.
Elements have weight, throwing them works, they settle rather than snap, and they
occupy space that other elements respect. Nothing uses a duration; everything uses
a stiffness. **Implies** a physics loop, spring tokens instead of easing curves,
pointer velocity capture, a resting-state layout that is valid. **Fails** as a toy
when the physics never resolves into something readable.
**Right when** the work is interactive and the play makes a point.

**Scroll-cinema.** The page is a film reel scrubbed by the scrollbar. Scroll position
maps to a timeline, sections pin while their contents advance, and the sequence has
shots, cuts, and a cadence. Progress is authored rather than emergent.
**Implies** pinned scroll containers, scrubbed timelines, `will-change` discipline,
preloaded frames, a real budget under `§13`. **Fails** as hijacked scroll that fights
the user's input and strands anyone who lands mid-page.
**Right when** the work has narrative order and one story to tell.

**Spatial / 3D-world.** The site is a navigable space with camera, depth, and
position. Sections are places, navigation is movement, and the user's sense of where
they are does the work a menu usually does. **Implies** WebGL or CSS 3D, a camera
rig, level-of-detail, a no-WebGL fallback per `§12`, an aggressive heavy-layer
budget. **Fails** as a maze where the user cannot find the case study, which is `§7`
violated structurally. **Right when** the work is spatial and a flat page would
misrepresent it.

## Technical and data

**Terminal.** Monospace throughout, a real fixed cell grid, blinking block cursor,
phosphor color on near-black, scanlines and slight CRT curvature at the edges.
Interaction is command-shaped, and output appears in a scrollback that persists.
**Implies** `ch` units, monospace with real box-drawing coverage, a CRT shader,
typed-output timing. **Fails** as a gimmick with a fake prompt that accepts three
commands and breaks on the fourth. **Right when** the subject is infrastructure,
security, or systems, and the terminal is where their work actually happens.

**Blueprint.** Technical drawing conventions applied literally: dimension lines with
arrowheads and measurements, section callouts, leader lines to annotations, hatching,
a title block in the corner, and a consistent line-weight hierarchy. Color is
reserved for the drawing ground. **Implies** SVG line work, precise stroke tokens,
annotation positioning, a monospace or drafting typeface.
**Fails** as decoration when the dimensions are fake and measure nothing real.
**Right when** the subject builds physical or architectural things and the callouts
can annotate actual work.

**Data-brutalist.** Dense tables, sparklines, and charts presented as the aesthetic
rather than supporting evidence. Rules are hairlines, numbers are tabular, alignment
is decimal, and the visual interest comes from the density of true information.
**Implies** `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, real table semantics, inline SVG
charts, a hairline border token. **Fails** the moment the numbers are decorative,
which is `§5` broken outright. **Right when** the subject's work produces real
numbers and the evidence file can carry every one of them.

**Wireframe / vector.** Line art only: no fills, hidden-line removal, contours and
edges describing volume through stroke alone. Objects read as constructed rather
than rendered, with weight variation carrying depth.
**Implies** SVG or WebGL line rendering, hidden-line computation, stroke-only tokens,
draw-on animation. **Fails** as thin and cold at small sizes where strokes vanish.
**Right when** the subject's work is structural and the outline is the honest view.

## Textural

**Risograph.** Two or three spot inks printed in separate passes with visible
misregistration, halftone dots in the shadows, ink that sits on the paper surface,
and paper grain showing through everywhere. Overprint areas produce a third color
that neither ink has alone. **Implies** channel-separated layers, `mix-blend-mode:
multiply`, offset per channel, halftone shader, a paper texture generated per `§10`.
**Fails** as a filter when the misregistration is uniform, since real registration
error drifts. **Right when** the subject is an illustrator, printer, or publisher.

**Xerox / degraded.** Photocopy artifacts as the medium: blown-out highlights,
crushed blacks, toner scatter at the edges, a slight skew, and visible generational
loss where a copy of a copy has lost its midtones. Contrast is brutal and
intermediate values barely exist. **Implies** threshold and dither passes, noise
displacement, per-element skew, a high-contrast duotone.
**Fails** as illegible when applied to body copy rather than to images and headers.
**Right when** the subject's work is zine, punk, or archival.

**Collage.** Layered scraps at mixed scale with torn edges, tape and staple
attachments, cast shadows from real height differences, and elements rotated off
axis. Scale jumps hard between layers, and the composition is assembled rather than
laid out. **Implies** irregular SVG masks, per-element shadow and rotation,
generated paper and tape textures, deliberate z-order.
**Fails** as chaos with no reading order, which loses `§6` immediately.
**Right when** the subject's practice is genuinely multidisciplinary.

**Ink / sumi.** Brush dynamics as the entire visual language: strokes with real
pressure variation, wet bleed into fiber, dry-brush breakup at speed, and negative
space treated as the subject rather than the leftover. One color, one gesture per
composition. **Implies** SVG variable-width paths, bleed via displacement, generated
fiber, animation that follows stroke order. **Fails** as a stock brush texture, which
reads as clip art instantly. **Right when** restraint is the position and the
subject's work rewards silence.

## Reductive

**Radical minimalism.** Type and space, nothing else. No borders, no cards, no
shadows, no illustration; hierarchy comes only from size, weight, and distance.
Every remaining element has to justify its existence, and the whitespace is measured
rather than left over. **Implies** one type family with real weights, a precise
spatial scale, perfect optical alignment, motion measured in single properties.
**Fails** as empty and unmemorable when the copy is weak, since there is nothing else
to look at. **Right when** the writing is strong and the work needs no frame.

**Monochrome plus one accent.** A single hue's full tonal range carries structure,
and exactly one accent, sampled from reality per `§8`, appears only where attention
must go. The discipline is that the accent never decorates.
**Implies** a lightness ramp in OKLCH, one accent token, strict usage rules in
`DIRECTION.md`. **Fails** as safe and forgettable, the most common way a run looks
competent and generic at once. **Right when** it is the discipline layer under a
louder collision partner.

**ASCII / text-only.** The page is characters. Art is drawn in a fixed cell grid,
layout is built from box-drawing glyphs, and images are dithered into character
density. Nothing is rendered that could not be pasted into a text file.
**Implies** monospace with full box-drawing coverage, `ch` and `lh` units,
image-to-ASCII conversion, semantic HTML underneath the art per `§12`.
**Fails** as unreadable to screen readers and unusable below 400px.
**Right when** the constraint is the point and the subject's audience reads it as one.

---

## Collision

This is the most important section in the file. A single named style is one search
away from being everyone else's site; the un-templated work lives where two styles
are held in tension. A collision produces properties neither parent has, because the
constraints of one force the other to behave in ways its own tradition never asks of
it.

| Collision | What it produces that neither parent has |
|---|---|
| **Liquid glass over a blueprint substrate** | A technical drawing is flat and authoritative by convention. Put a refractive lens over it and the dimension lines bend as you scroll, so precision becomes something you look *through*. The drawing gains depth without losing its claim to accuracy. |
| **Risograph texture on a Swiss grid** | The grid asserts machine order; the misregistration asserts a hand and a press. Together they read as a printed object rather than a rendered page, and the grid stops looking like every other agency site because it is visibly ink. |
| **Terminal chrome around a physics world** | The monospace frame promises determinism and fixed cells. The contents obey springs and collide. The tension between a frame that cannot bend and contents that will not sit still is the whole idea, and neither style contains it alone. |
| **Editorial print with a spatial 3D reveal** | Columns, drop caps, marginalia, then the page turns out to have depth and the columns are planes standing in space. Reading becomes navigation, and the reader's position in the document becomes literal. |
| **Brutalist structure with a cinematic grade** | Raw exposed structure and system fonts, lit with a single key and a vignette. The honesty stops reading as unfinished and starts reading as staged, which is a claim neither raw HTML nor a film grade makes on its own. |
| **Neumorphism inside radical minimalism** | The style that normally fails by covering a page in soft mush is reduced to one extruded object in an empty field. It becomes sculptural, and the contrast failure disappears because nothing needs to be read off it. |
| **Ink gesture across data-brutalism** | Dense tabular numbers with one brush stroke laid over them. The gesture asserts that a person read these numbers and had a view, which a table cannot say and a painting cannot evidence. |
| **Vaporwave chrome under Swiss typography** | Y2K materials disciplined by an unforgiving grid and one type family. The nostalgia survives, the kitsch collapse does not, because the layout refuses to join in. |

**Picking a collision that serves the brief.** One parent comes from the archetype and
positioning in `BRAND.md`. The other comes from something materially true about the
subject: their medium, their tools, the physical object their work becomes, the room
they work in. Both parents must be defensible in one sentence each against
`BRIEF.md`. If only one is defensible, you have a style plus a decoration, and the
decoration will read as arbitrary to everyone who sees it.

**The load-bearing rule:** one parent carries structure, the other carries surface.
Two structural parents fight over the grid and produce mush. Two surface parents
produce noise with no bones. Name which parent is which in `DIRECTION.md` before you
build anything.

## Subversion

The second route out of template. Take one style and break exactly one of its own
rules, and the rule you break has to be the one the style is most identified by.
Break two and you have a different style executed badly.

- **Swiss where one element never obeys the grid.** A single photographic plate hangs
  past the margin in every section, at the same overhang each time. The grid is
  provable everywhere else, which is what makes the overhang read as a decision.
- **Brutalism with immaculate type.** Everything raw, default, unstyled, except the
  typography, which is set with real optical sizing, hyphenation, and hung
  punctuation. The refusal to decorate becomes selective and therefore intentional.
- **Cinematic dark that turns the lights on once.** One section, usually the contact
  or the about, drops the grade entirely and goes flat daylight white. The return to
  darkness afterwards hits harder than the darkness ever did alone.
- **Glassmorphism with no blur.** The panels refract and catch light at their edges
  and nothing behind them is softened. Legibility improves, `§12` gets easier, and
  the material reads as harder and more precise than glass usually does.
- **Editorial print where the margin is the main column.** Marginalia carries the
  primary narrative and the body text becomes the aside. The reader's eye learns a
  new hierarchy in about four seconds and remembers it.
- **Terminal with one full-color photograph.** Everything is phosphor and monospace
  except a single image rendered at full fidelity. It becomes the most important
  object on the site without any layout emphasis at all.

State the broken rule explicitly in `DIRECTION.md`. A subversion nobody can name is
indistinguishable from an inconsistency.

## The guardrails

This section is `§3` enforced.

- **The vocabulary names a starting position, never a destination.** Ship a named
  style unmodified and the run failed. There is no entry in this file that is a
  finished answer.
- **Every run states in `DIRECTION.md` what it did to the style that nobody else
  does** — the collision, the subversion, or the invention applied, in one sentence
  a stranger could check the site against.
- **The vision beats the style.** If `VISION` or `BRIEF.md` says "quiet, like a
  printed book," liquid glass is off the table regardless of how good the prototype
  looks. A prototype is not an argument against the intake from `§0`.
- **The archetype from `BRAND.md` pulls a shortlist, never a single answer.** An
  archetype narrows the field to three or four candidates. Treating it as a lookup
  table is how every Sage becomes Swiss and every Creator becomes neo-brutalist.
- **Anti-positioning from `BRAND.md` bans styles outright.** If the strategy says
  "never look like a crypto site," glow-neon and chrome are gone. Honor it
  absolutely, the same way `§0` do-nots are honored.
- **The list is open.** Invent one, name it, describe it in the format above, and add
  it to the run. An invented style with a real name and stated mechanics beats the
  best-executed entry on this page, because nobody can pattern-match it.

## Style and accessibility

`§12` is **[HARD]**. These styles fight it hardest, and each ships with its fix or
does not ship.

| Style | What it fights | The fix that ships |
|---|---|---|
| **Neumorphism** | Form is shadow on one hue, so nothing has a contrast ratio | Extrusion is for containers only. Every label, value, and control state gets a real foreground token measured at ≥4.5:1. Focus is a hard visible ring, never a deeper shadow. |
| **Glassmorphism / liquid glass** | Text contrast changes with whatever scrolls behind it | An opaque or near-opaque scrim behind every text run, measured against the *worst* frame of the moving substrate rather than a screenshot. |
| **Cinematic dark** | Vignette, grade, and grain push small type below threshold | Measure contrast on the rendered pixels after grade and grain, not on the tokens. Body copy stays out of the vignette falloff. Grain opacity drops on text layers. |
| **Kinetic / physics / scroll-cinema** | Motion is the design, so removing motion removes the site | An art-directed still per `§12`: a composed frame with type at rest that someone designed. Scroll-cinema degrades to a paginated document with the same content in the same order. |
| **Spatial / 3D-world** | Navigation depends on a camera and a GPU | Keyboard traversal between named places, a text route to every section, and a no-WebGL fallback that is a real page rather than an apology. |
| **Terminal** | Scanlines and CRT curvature reduce legibility and can trigger | Curvature and scanline opacity behind `prefers-reduced-motion` plus a visible toggle. Body text renders on the flat layer above the effect. |
| **ASCII / text-only** | Screen readers read the art as character soup | `aria-hidden` on the art, `role="img"` with a written alt on the block, and real semantic HTML carrying the actual content underneath. |
| **Glow-neon / vaporwave** | Saturated emission on dark causes halation and fringing | Glow applies to non-text elements only. Text uses a desaturated stop of the same hue at full contrast. Chromatic aberration never touches a glyph. |
| **Data-brutalist** | Density defeats zoom and reflow | Real table semantics with scoped headers, horizontal scroll containers that are keyboard reachable, and a stated minimum readable width. |

## Light and dark as two designs

Per [`CRAFT.md`](./CRAFT.md)'s art-directed modes, a style often needs a genuinely
different treatment in each mode. Never `filter: invert()`. Choose per-mode ink,
substrate, shadow direction, and accent chroma deliberately.

These break under naive inversion:

- **Neumorphism.** Inverting the shadow pair puts the light source underneath, which
  no physical object does. Keep the light direction identical in both modes and
  change only the surface hue and the shadow spread.
- **Glassmorphism.** Blur reads as depth on dark and as haze on light. The light mode
  needs more opacity, a heavier border, and less blur to say the same thing.
- **Cinematic dark.** There is no light version of a lit set. The light mode is a
  second art direction: a printed still with the grade baked in as a duotone, no
  vignette, no bloom.
- **Glow / neon.** Emission requires darkness. In light mode, glow becomes ink
  saturation and weight, and the accent moves from emissive to dense.
- **Risograph.** Paper is the substrate. Dark mode is a black-paper print run with
  different inks chosen for it, and the halftone dot inverts to open rather than
  filled.
- **Blueprint.** White-on-blue and blue-on-white are both real print conventions.
  Switch between the two on purpose, with line weights retuned, since hairlines that
  read on dark disappear on white.
- **Aurora / mesh.** OKLCH interpolation that stays saturated on dark goes chalky on
  light. Each mode needs its own stop list, not a lightness shift.

Declare in `DIRECTION.md` whether the two modes are one design in two palettes or two
art directions. If the chosen style appears on the list above, the answer is two art
directions, and both get built and screenshotted under `§14`.

# Styles

This file is the visual vocabulary: **what it looks like**. [`CRAFT.md`](./CRAFT.md)
is the technique arsenal: **how you render it**. They are separate on purpose, and
collapsing them is how runs end up templated.

The distinction is sharp because techniques carry no opinion. `backdrop-filter`
builds the layered translucency of liquid glass, and it also builds the flat frosted
panels of a Swiss layout where the blur is the only softness on the page. A noise
shader is film grain in a cinematic grade and paper tooth in a risograph print. A
spring is playful in a claymorphic world and clinical in a blueprint. The style is
the opinion; the technique is a means of getting there.

The order is fixed. **Style is chosen at Gate B1 with the concept**, from the brief,
the archetype, and the vision. **Techniques are assigned in Loop 2b to serve the
style already chosen.** Reaching for a style because you want to use a shader is the
tail wagging the dog, and it shows in the output.

Everything below is a starting position under `§3`. Read
[the guardrails](#the-guardrails) before you pick.

---

## Surface and material

**Glassmorphism.** Translucent panels floating over a substrate worth seeing through
to, legible because of the blur behind them rather than a fill. Depth reads as blur
radius, nearest layer blurring hardest, each panel edged with a 1px light-catching
border. **Implies** `backdrop-filter`, deliberate z-layering, `color-mix()` borders,
a live substrate. **Fails** as gray rectangles when the background is flat, and fails
`§12` when body copy sits on moving translucency. **Right when** depth is the message
and the background is itself content.

**Liquid glass.** Apple's 2025 material language, where the panel refracts rather
than merely blurs: content bends as it passes under the edge, specular highlights
track a light source, and the shape lenses during scroll. Real implementation is an
SDF and shader job with normals and a refraction pass; `backdrop-filter` alone gets
you glassmorphism with a borrowed name. **Implies** WebGL, an SDF for the panel,
scroll-linked light, a hard `§13` budget. **Fails** as chrome that buries the work
(`§7`) and stutters on mid-range Android. **Right when** the subject's work is
material or hardware and the budget is declared.

**Neumorphism / soft UI.** Every element extruded from one background hue by a
matched shadow pair, one dark and one light, cast from a single committed angle.
No borders and almost no color: form is entirely shadow, in one narrow tonal band.
It fails contrast by default and only ships with the fix in
[Style and accessibility](#style-and-accessibility). **Implies** dual `box-shadow`,
one hue with lightness variation. **Fails** as a field of putty with invisible
affordances. **Right when** exactly one object is extruded and the rest is flat.

**Claymorphism.** Inflated rounded volumes with large radii, soft occlusion at the
base, and a bright saturated palette. Objects read as pressable toys with real
thickness, lifted by a diffuse colored shadow, with heavy rounded type to match.
**Implies** big `border-radius`, layered colored shadows, spring press, generous
padding. **Fails** as childish, which sinks a senior portfolio faster than anything
else here. **Right when** the work is consumer or game-adjacent and the copy carries
the seriousness.

**Skeuomorphic revival.** Real material simulation rather than nostalgic gloss: paper
with visible fiber, ink bleeding into it, embossed metal with a directional brush,
edges worn where a thumb rests. One material, simulated honestly, physics respected
everywhere. **Implies** generated textures per `§10`, displacement and grain maps,
per-material lighting. **Fails** as 2010 iOS pastiche the moment two materials share
a surface without a reason. **Right when** the work has a physical antecedent that
can be named in one word.

**Aerogel / frosted depth.** Translucency without a light source: milky diffuse
layers where depth reads as accumulated haze and nothing has a hard edge. Separation
comes from density, the palette stays desaturated, and light bleeds between planes.
**Implies** stacked low-opacity fills, large soft blurs, a fog gradient, near-zero
border weight. **Fails** as washed-out mush when every layer sits at one density.
**Right when** the work is atmospheric and hierarchy can ride on type alone.

## Structural

**Swiss / International.** A visible modular grid, one family at a strict scale,
flush-left ragged-right setting, objective photography on grid intersections.
Whitespace is structural, color appears once, every alignment is provable against
the column. **Implies** CSS Grid with named lines, a mathematical type scale,
baseline rhythm, one accent from `§8`. **Fails** as an agency template, since it is
the most-copied system in design. **Right when** the work is dense and needs an
authoritative frame, and only with a collision or subversion applied.

**Brutalism.** Raw HTML honesty: system fonts, default link blue, visible borders,
unstyled form controls. The page looks like the document it is, with layout that
reveals the DOM rather than disguising it. **Implies** near-zero CSS, system font
stacks, native controls, no motion. **Fails** as an excuse for laziness,
indistinguishable from an unfinished build. **Right when** credibility comes from
substance and the refusal to decorate is itself the position.

**Neo-brutalism.** Thick black borders, hard offset shadows with no blur, saturated
flat blocks, heavy grotesque type at aggressive sizes. Elements sit at slight
rotations and overlap without softening; interaction moves the shadow rather than
fading anything. **Implies** solid `box-shadow` offsets, 2–4px borders, transform on
hover, a loud limited palette. **Fails** as Gumroad cosplay, the most saturated style
on the web right now. **Right when** the subject is loud and the collision partner
supplies the restraint.

**Bento.** A dense grid of unequal self-contained cards sized by importance rather
than content length, with uniform radii and consistent gaps, reading as one object at
a glance. **Implies** CSS Grid with spanning areas, container queries, per-card art
direction, a strict radius token. **Fails** as a dashboard with nothing to show, and
hides narrative because every card is equal in reading order. **Right when** the
subject has many small things worth seeing simultaneously.

**Editorial / print.** Magazine mechanics carried honestly onto screen: measured
columns, real hyphenation, drop caps on the baseline grid, pull quotes breaking the
measure, marginalia in the outer column, running heads and folios. Type does the
work; images are plates. **Implies** `hyphens`, `text-wrap: pretty`,
`initial-letter`, multi-column at desktop only, a serif with optical sizes,
self-hosted per `§9`. **Fails** past a 75-character measure or when columns force
scroll-up reading on mobile. **Right when** the case studies are long.

**Swiss-punk / Ray Gun.** The Swiss grid built, then deliberately violated: type
overlapping, rotated, set in conflicting families, letters cropped by the viewport.
Type becomes image and legibility becomes a variable the designer controls.
**Implies** absolute positioning over a grid, `mix-blend-mode`, variable-font
extremes, cropped SVG text. **Fails** as noise when the underlying grid was never
actually built, since the violation only reads against visible order. **Right when**
the audience reads visual sophistication.

## Atmospheric

**Cinematic dark.** A single key light with real falloff, deep vignette, grain sized
to the viewport, and a graded palette where the blacks are lifted and tinted.
Content sits in pools of light and the space between them is genuinely dark.
**Implies** radial key, grain shader or SVG turbulence, LUT via `feColorMatrix`,
controlled bloom. **Fails** when the grade crushes body copy below 4.5:1 and grain
eats small type. **Right when** the work is visual and benefits from being lit.

**Aurora / mesh gradient.** Large soft color fields drifting across each other with
no visible edges and no repeat. OKLCH interpolation keeps the midpoints saturated
instead of going gray, and motion is slow enough to be felt without being watched.
**Implies** OKLCH gradients, canvas or WebGL mesh, long-period animation, grain to
defeat banding. **Fails** as the default AI landing page, the most generated look of
the last three years. **Right when** it is a substrate for another style rather than
the style itself.

**Glow / neon.** A dark substrate with emissive accents that actually bloom, light
spilling past its source and tinting what it lands on. Edges glow from the inside,
shadows take the accent hue, two emissive colors at most. **Implies** layered
`box-shadow` bloom or a real bloom pass, dark tokens, hue-matched shadows.
**Fails** as halation that makes every string of text fringe. **Right when** the work
is nocturnal or technical and the emission points at the work.

**Vaporwave / Y2K.** Chromed type with environment reflection, cyan and magenta
gradient meshes, CRT scanlines and phosphor bleed, grids receding to a horizon,
deliberate JPEG and VHS artifacts. The nostalgia is specific to 1995–2003 hardware
and reads as costume unless committed to fully. **Implies** SVG chrome gradients, a
CRT shader, chromatic aberration, dithering, a period type pairing. **Fails** as
kitsch that dates the subject. **Right when** the audience shares the reference.

**Solarpunk.** Organic growth forms and botanical geometry under warm optimistic
light: curves derived from phyllotaxis rather than arbitrary blobs, terracotta and
sage and brass, layouts that branch rather than stack. **Implies** generative SVG
growth, warm gradients, curved layout paths, organic easing. **Fails** as generic
eco-branding with a leaf icon and a green button. **Right when** the work is climate,
agriculture, health, or civic.

## Motion-native

In these four the behavior **is** the aesthetic. A still screenshot cannot represent
them, which makes the `§12` reduced-motion design a first-class deliverable.

**Kinetic.** Nothing is at rest: type in perpetual motion, marquees running at
different rates by depth, letters responding to pointer velocity, composition
recomposing continuously. Stillness is used once, as punctuation. **Implies**
scroll-velocity input, variable-font axis animation, `requestAnimationFrame`,
transform-only compositing. **Fails** as exhausting, and unreadable when the thing in
motion is the thing being read. **Right when** the work is performance or sound.

**Physics-world.** Spring, inertia, mass, and collision are the interaction model.
Elements have weight, throwing them works, they settle rather than snap, and they
occupy space other elements respect. Nothing uses a duration; everything uses a
stiffness. **Implies** a physics loop, spring tokens instead of easing curves,
pointer velocity capture, a valid resting layout. **Fails** as a toy when the physics
never resolves into something readable. **Right when** the play makes a point.

**Scroll-cinema.** The page is a film reel scrubbed by the scrollbar: scroll position
maps to a timeline, sections pin while their contents advance, and the sequence has
shots, cuts, and cadence. **Implies** pinned containers, scrubbed timelines,
`will-change` discipline, preloaded frames, a real `§13` budget. **Fails** as
hijacked scroll that fights the user and strands anyone landing mid-page.
**Right when** the work has narrative order and one story to tell.

**Spatial / 3D-world.** The site is a navigable space with camera, depth, and
position. Sections are places, navigation is movement, and the sense of where you are
does the work a menu usually does. **Implies** WebGL or CSS 3D, a camera rig,
level-of-detail, a no-WebGL fallback per `§12`, an aggressive budget. **Fails** as a
maze where nobody finds the case study, which is `§7` violated structurally.
**Right when** a flat page would misrepresent the work.

## Technical and data

**Terminal.** Monospace throughout on a real fixed cell grid, blinking block cursor,
phosphor color on near-black, scanlines and slight CRT curvature at the edges.
Interaction is command-shaped and output persists in scrollback. **Implies** `ch`
units, a monospace with box-drawing coverage, a CRT shader, typed-output timing.
**Fails** as a gimmick with a fake prompt that accepts three commands and breaks on
the fourth. **Right when** the terminal is where the subject's work actually happens.

**Blueprint.** Drawing conventions applied literally: dimension lines with arrowheads
and measurements, section callouts, leader lines to annotations, hatching, a title
block, and a consistent line-weight hierarchy. Color is reserved for the ground.
**Implies** SVG line work, precise stroke tokens, annotation positioning, a drafting
typeface. **Fails** as decoration when the dimensions are fake and measure nothing.
**Right when** the callouts annotate actual work.

**Data-brutalist.** Dense tables, sparklines, and charts presented as the aesthetic
rather than as supporting evidence. Rules are hairlines, numbers are tabular,
alignment is decimal, and the interest comes from the density of true information.
**Implies** `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, real table semantics, inline SVG
charts. **Fails** the moment the numbers are decorative, which breaks `§5` outright.
**Right when** `EVIDENCE.md` can carry every number on the page.

**Wireframe / vector.** Line art only: no fills, hidden-line removal, contours and
edges describing volume through stroke alone, with weight variation carrying depth.
Objects read as constructed. **Implies** SVG or WebGL line rendering, hidden-line
computation, stroke-only tokens, draw-on animation. **Fails** as thin and cold at
sizes where strokes vanish. **Right when** the work is structural and the outline is
the honest view.

## Textural

**Risograph.** Two or three spot inks printed in separate passes with visible
misregistration, halftone dots in the shadows, and paper grain showing through.
Overprint areas produce a third color neither ink has alone. **Implies**
channel-separated layers, `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, per-channel offset, a halftone
shader, paper texture generated per `§10`. **Fails** as a filter when the
misregistration is uniform, since real registration error drifts. **Right when** the
subject is an illustrator, printer, or publisher.

**Xerox / degraded.** Photocopy artifacts as the medium: blown highlights, crushed
blacks, toner scatter at the edges, a slight skew, and generational loss where a copy
of a copy has lost its midtones. Contrast is brutal and midtones barely exist.
**Implies** threshold and dither passes, noise displacement, per-element skew, a
high-contrast duotone. **Fails** as illegible when applied to body copy rather than
to images and headers. **Right when** the work is zine, punk, or archival.

**Collage.** Layered scraps at mixed scale with torn edges, tape and staples, cast
shadows from real height differences, and elements rotated off axis. Scale jumps hard
between layers and the composition is assembled rather than laid out. **Implies**
irregular SVG masks, per-element shadow and rotation, generated paper and tape,
deliberate z-order. **Fails** as chaos with no reading order, losing `§6` immediately.
**Right when** the subject's practice is genuinely multidisciplinary.

**Ink / sumi.** Brush dynamics as the whole language: strokes with real pressure
variation, wet bleed into fiber, dry-brush breakup at speed, negative space treated
as the subject. One color, one gesture per composition. **Implies** SVG
variable-width paths, bleed via displacement, generated fiber, animation following
stroke order. **Fails** as a stock brush texture, which reads as clip art instantly.
**Right when** restraint is the position and the work rewards silence.

## Reductive

**Radical minimalism.** Type and space, nothing else: no borders, no cards, no
shadows, no illustration. Hierarchy comes only from size, weight, and distance, and
the whitespace is measured rather than left over. **Implies** one family with real
weights, a precise spatial scale, optical alignment, single-property motion.
**Fails** as empty and unmemorable when the copy is weak, since there is nothing else
to look at. **Right when** the writing is strong and the work needs no frame.

**Monochrome plus one accent.** A single hue's full tonal range carries structure,
and exactly one accent sampled from reality per `§8` appears only where attention
must go. The discipline is that the accent never decorates. **Implies** an OKLCH
lightness ramp, one accent token, usage rules stated in `DIRECTION.md`. **Fails** as
forgettable, the most common way a run looks competent and generic at once.
**Right when** it is the discipline layer under a louder collision partner.

**ASCII / text-only.** The page is characters: art drawn in a fixed cell grid, layout
built from box-drawing glyphs, images dithered into character density. Nothing is
rendered that could not be pasted into a text file. **Implies** monospace with full
box-drawing coverage, `ch` and `lh` units, image-to-ASCII conversion, semantic HTML
underneath per `§12`. **Fails** as unreadable to screen readers and unusable below
400px. **Right when** the constraint is the point and the audience reads it as one.

---

## Collision

This is the most important section in the file. A single named style is one search
away from being everyone else's site. The un-templated work lives where two styles
are held in tension, because the constraints of one force the other to behave in ways
its own tradition never asks of it.

| Collision | What it produces that neither parent has |
|---|---|
| **Liquid glass over a blueprint substrate** | A technical drawing is flat and authoritative by convention. Put a refractive lens over it and the dimension lines bend as you scroll, so precision becomes something you look *through*. The drawing gains depth without losing its claim to accuracy. |
| **Risograph texture on a Swiss grid** | The grid asserts machine order; the misregistration asserts a hand and a press. Together they read as a printed object rather than a rendered page, and the grid stops looking like every other agency site because it is visibly ink. |
| **Terminal chrome around a physics world** | The monospace frame promises determinism and fixed cells. The contents obey springs and collide. A frame that cannot bend around contents that will not sit still is the whole idea, and neither style contains it alone. |
| **Editorial print with a spatial 3D reveal** | Columns, drop caps, marginalia, then the page turns out to have depth and the columns are planes standing in space. Reading becomes navigation and the reader's position in the document becomes literal. |
| **Brutalist structure with a cinematic grade** | Raw exposed structure and system fonts, lit with a single key and a vignette. The honesty stops reading as unfinished and starts reading as staged, a claim neither raw HTML nor a film grade makes on its own. |
| **Neumorphism inside radical minimalism** | The style that normally fails by covering a page in soft mush is reduced to one extruded object in an empty field. It becomes sculptural, and the contrast failure disappears because nothing has to be read off it. |
| **Ink gesture across data-brutalism** | Dense tabular numbers with one brush stroke laid over them. The gesture asserts that a person read these numbers and had a view, which a table cannot say and a painting cannot evidence. |
| **Vaporwave chrome under Swiss typography** | Y2K materials disciplined by an unforgiving grid and one type family. The nostalgia survives, the kitsch collapse does not, because the layout refuses to join in. |

**Picking a collision that serves the brief.** One parent comes from the archetype and
positioning in `BRAND.md`. The other comes from something materially true about the
subject: their medium, their tools, the physical object their work becomes, the room
they work in. Both parents must be defensible in one sentence each against
`BRIEF.md`. If only one is defensible, you have a style plus a decoration, and the
decoration reads as arbitrary to everyone who sees it.

**The load-bearing rule:** one parent carries structure, the other carries surface.
Two structural parents fight over the grid and produce mush. Two surface parents
produce noise with no bones. Name which parent is which in `DIRECTION.md` before you
build anything.

## Subversion

The second route out of template. Take one style and break exactly one of its own
rules, and the rule you break has to be the one the style is most identified by.
Break two and you have a different style executed badly.

- **Swiss where one element never obeys the grid.** A single photographic plate hangs
  past the margin in every section, at the same overhang each time. The grid is
  provable everywhere else, which is what makes the overhang read as a decision.
- **Brutalism with immaculate type.** Everything raw, default, unstyled, except the
  typography, which gets real optical sizing, hyphenation, and hung punctuation. The
  refusal to decorate becomes selective and therefore intentional.
- **Cinematic dark that turns the lights on once.** One section drops the grade
  entirely and goes flat daylight white. The return to darkness afterwards hits
  harder than the darkness ever did alone.
- **Glassmorphism with no blur.** The panels refract and catch light at their edges
  and nothing behind them softens. Legibility improves, `§12` gets easier, and the
  material reads as harder and more precise than glass usually does.
- **Editorial print where the margin is the main column.** Marginalia carries the
  primary narrative and the body text becomes the aside. The reader learns a new
  hierarchy in about four seconds and remembers it.
- **Terminal with one full-color photograph.** Everything is phosphor and monospace
  except a single image at full fidelity. It becomes the most important object on the
  site with no layout emphasis at all.

State the broken rule explicitly in `DIRECTION.md`. A subversion nobody can name is
indistinguishable from an inconsistency.

## The guardrails

This section is `§3` enforced.

- **The vocabulary names a starting position, never a destination.** Ship a named
  style unmodified and the run failed. No entry above is a finished answer.
- **Every run states in `DIRECTION.md` what it did to the style that nobody else
  does** — the collision, subversion, or invention applied, in one sentence a
  stranger could check the site against.
- **The vision beats the style.** If the vision or `BRIEF.md` says "quiet, like a
  printed book," liquid glass is off the table regardless of how good the prototype
  looks. A prototype is not an argument against the intake from `§0`.
- **The archetype from `BRAND.md` pulls a shortlist, never a single answer.** It
  narrows the field to three or four candidates. Treating it as a lookup table is how
  every Sage becomes Swiss and every Creator becomes neo-brutalist.
- **Anti-positioning from `BRAND.md` bans styles outright.** If the strategy says
  "never look like a crypto site," glow-neon and chrome are gone. Honor it as
  absolutely as the `§0` do-nots.
- **The list is open.** Invent one, name it, describe it in the format above, and add
  it to the run. An invented style with a real name and stated mechanics beats the
  best-executed entry on this page, because nobody can pattern-match it.

## Style and accessibility

`§12` is **[HARD]**. These styles fight it hardest, and each ships with its fix or
does not ship.

| Style | What it fights | The fix that ships |
|---|---|---|
| **Neumorphism** | Form is shadow on one hue, so nothing has a contrast ratio | Extrusion is for containers only. Every label, value, and control state gets a real foreground token at ≥4.5:1. Focus is a hard visible ring, never a deeper shadow. |
| **Glassmorphism / liquid glass** | Text contrast changes with whatever scrolls behind it | An opaque or near-opaque scrim behind every text run, measured against the *worst* frame of the moving substrate rather than a screenshot. |
| **Cinematic dark** | Vignette, grade, and grain push small type below threshold | Measure contrast on the rendered pixels after grade and grain, not on the tokens. Body copy stays out of the vignette falloff. Grain opacity drops on text layers. |
| **Kinetic / physics / scroll-cinema** | Motion is the design, so removing motion removes the site | An art-directed still per `§12`: a composed frame with type at rest that someone designed. Scroll-cinema degrades to a paginated document, same content, same order. |
| **Spatial / 3D-world** | Navigation depends on a camera and a GPU | Keyboard traversal between named places, a text route to every section, and a no-WebGL fallback that is a real page rather than an apology. |
| **Terminal** | Scanlines and CRT curvature reduce legibility and can trigger | Curvature and scanline opacity behind `prefers-reduced-motion` plus a visible toggle. Body text renders on the flat layer above the effect. |
| **ASCII / text-only** | Screen readers read the art as character soup | `aria-hidden` on the art, `role="img"` with a written alt on the block, and real semantic HTML carrying the content underneath. |
| **Glow-neon / vaporwave** | Saturated emission on dark causes halation and fringing | Glow applies to non-text elements only. Text uses a desaturated stop of the same hue at full contrast. Chromatic aberration never touches a glyph. |
| **Data-brutalist** | Density defeats zoom and reflow | Real table semantics with scoped headers, horizontal scroll containers that are keyboard reachable, and a stated minimum readable width. |

## Light and dark as two designs

Per [`CRAFT.md`](./CRAFT.md)'s art-directed modes, a style often needs a genuinely
different treatment in each mode. Never `filter: invert()`. Choose per-mode ink,
substrate, shadow direction, and accent chroma deliberately. These break under naive
inversion:

- **Neumorphism.** Inverting the shadow pair puts the light source underneath, which
  no physical object does. Keep the light direction identical in both modes and
  change only the surface hue and the shadow spread.
- **Glassmorphism.** Blur reads as depth on dark and as haze on light. Light mode
  needs more opacity, a heavier border, and less blur to say the same thing.
- **Cinematic dark.** There is no light version of a lit set. Light mode is a second
  art direction: a printed still with the grade baked in as a duotone, no vignette,
  no bloom.
- **Glow / neon.** Emission requires darkness. In light mode the glow becomes ink
  saturation and weight, and the accent moves from emissive to dense.
- **Risograph.** Paper is the substrate. Dark mode is a black-paper print run with
  inks chosen for it, and the halftone dot inverts to open rather than filled.
- **Blueprint.** White-on-blue and blue-on-white are both real print conventions.
  Switch between them on purpose, with line weights retuned, since hairlines that
  read on dark disappear on white.
- **Aurora / mesh.** OKLCH stops that stay saturated on dark go chalky on light. Each
  mode needs its own stop list rather than a lightness shift.

Declare in `DIRECTION.md` whether the two modes are one design in two palettes or two
art directions. If the chosen style appears above, the answer is two art directions,
and both get built and screenshotted under `§14`.

# Styles

This file is the visual vocabulary: **what it looks like**. [`CRAFT.md`](./CRAFT.md)
is the technique arsenal: **how you render it**. They are separate on purpose, and
collapsing them is how runs end up templated.

The distinction is sharp because techniques carry no opinion. `backdrop-filter`
builds the layered translucency of liquid glass, and it also builds the flat frosted
panels of a Swiss layout where the blur is the only softness on the page. A noise
shader is film grain in a cinematic grade and paper tooth in a risograph print. A
spring is playful in a claymorphic world and clinical in a blueprint. The style is
the opinion; the technique is a means of getting there.

The order is fixed. **Style is chosen at Gate B1 with the concept**, from the brief,
the archetype, and the vision. **Techniques are assigned in Loop 2b to serve the
style already chosen.** Reaching for a style because you want to use a shader is the
tail wagging the dog, and it shows in the output.

Everything below is a starting position under `§3`. Read
[the guardrails](#the-guardrails) before you pick.

---

## Surface and material

**Glassmorphism.** Translucent panels floating over a substrate worth seeing through
to, legible because of the blur behind them rather than a fill. Depth reads as blur
radius, nearest layer blurring hardest, each panel edged with a 1px light-catching
border. **Implies** `backdrop-filter`, deliberate z-layering, `color-mix()` borders,
a live substrate. **Fails** as gray rectangles when the background is flat, and fails
`§12` when body copy sits on moving translucency. **Right when** depth is the message
and the background is itself content.

**Liquid glass.** Apple's 2025 material language, where the panel refracts rather
than merely blurs: content bends as it passes under the edge, specular highlights
track a light source, and the shape lenses during scroll. Real implementation is an
SDF and shader job with normals and a refraction pass; `backdrop-filter` alone gets
you glassmorphism with a borrowed name. **Implies** WebGL, an SDF for the panel,
scroll-linked light, a hard `§13` budget. **Fails** as chrome that buries the work
(`§7`) and stutters on mid-range Android. **Right when** the subject's work is
material or hardware and the budget is declared.

**Neumorphism / soft UI.** Every element extruded from one background hue by a
matched shadow pair, one dark and one light, cast from a single committed angle.
No borders and almost no color: form is entirely shadow, in one narrow tonal band.
It fails contrast by default and only ships with the fix in
[Style and accessibility](#style-and-accessibility). **Implies** dual `box-shadow`,
one hue with lightness variation. **Fails** as a field of putty with invisible
affordances. **Right when** exactly one object is extruded and the rest is flat.

**Claymorphism.** Inflated rounded volumes with large radii, soft occlusion at the
base, and a bright saturated palette. Objects read as pressable toys with real
thickness, lifted by a diffuse colored shadow, with heavy rounded type to match.
**Implies** big `border-radius`, layered colored shadows, spring press, generous
padding. **Fails** as childish, which sinks a senior portfolio faster than anything
else here. **Right when** the work is consumer or game-adjacent and the copy carries
the seriousness.

**Skeuomorphic revival.** Real material simulation rather than nostalgic gloss: paper
with visible fiber, ink bleeding into it, embossed metal with a directional brush,
edges worn where a thumb rests. One material, simulated honestly, physics respected
everywhere. **Implies** generated textures per `§10`, displacement and grain maps,
per-material lighting. **Fails** as 2010 iOS pastiche the moment two materials share
a surface without a reason. **Right when** the work has a physical antecedent that
can be named in one word.

**Aerogel / frosted depth.** Translucency without a light source: milky diffuse
layers where depth reads as accumulated haze and nothing has a hard edge. Separation
comes from density, the palette stays desaturated, and light bleeds between planes.
**Implies** stacked low-opacity fills, large soft blurs, a fog gradient, near-zero
border weight. **Fails** as washed-out mush when every layer sits at one density.
**Right when** the work is atmospheric and hierarchy can ride on type alone.

## Structural

**Swiss / International.** A visible modular grid, one family at a strict scale,
flush-left ragged-right setting, objective photography on grid intersections.
Whitespace is structural, color appears once, every alignment is provable against
the column. **Implies** CSS Grid with named lines, a mathematical type scale,
baseline rhythm, one accent from `§8`. **Fails** as an agency template, since it is
the most-copied system in design. **Right when** the work is dense and needs an
authoritative frame, and only with a collision or subversion applied.

**Brutalism.** Raw HTML honesty: system fonts, default link blue, visible borders,
unstyled form controls. The page looks like the document it is, with layout that
reveals the DOM rather than disguising it. **Implies** near-zero CSS, system font
stacks, native controls, no motion. **Fails** as an excuse for laziness,
indistinguishable from an unfinished build. **Right when** credibility comes from
substance and the refusal to decorate is itself the position.

**Neo-brutalism.** Thick black borders, hard offset shadows with no blur, saturated
flat blocks, heavy grotesque type at aggressive sizes. Elements sit at slight
rotations and overlap without softening; interaction moves the shadow rather than
fading anything. **Implies** solid `box-shadow` offsets, 2–4px borders, transform on
hover, a loud limited palette. **Fails** as Gumroad cosplay, the most saturated style
on the web right now. **Right when** the subject is loud and the collision partner
supplies the restraint.

**Bento.** A dense grid of unequal self-contained cards sized by importance rather
than content length, with uniform radii and consistent gaps, reading as one object at
a glance. **Implies** CSS Grid with spanning areas, container queries, per-card art
direction, a strict radius token. **Fails** as a dashboard with nothing to show, and
hides narrative because every card is equal in reading order. **Right when** the
subject has many small things worth seeing simultaneously.

**Editorial / print.** Magazine mechanics carried honestly onto screen: measured
columns, real hyphenation, drop caps on the baseline grid, pull quotes breaking the
measure, marginalia in the outer column, running heads and folios. Type does the
work; images are plates. **Implies** `hyphens`, `text-wrap: pretty`,
`initial-letter`, multi-column at desktop only, a serif with optical sizes,
self-hosted per `§9`. **Fails** past a 75-character measure or when columns force
scroll-up reading on mobile. **Right when** the case studies are long.

**Swiss-punk / Ray Gun.** The Swiss grid built, then deliberately violated: type
overlapping, rotated, set in conflicting families, letters cropped by the viewport.
Type becomes image and legibility becomes a variable the designer controls.
**Implies** absolute positioning over a grid, `mix-blend-mode`, variable-font
extremes, cropped SVG text. **Fails** as noise when the underlying grid was never
actually built, since the violation only reads against visible order. **Right when**
the audience reads visual sophistication.

## Atmospheric

**Cinematic dark.** A single key light with real falloff, deep vignette, grain sized
to the viewport, and a graded palette where the blacks are lifted and tinted.
Content sits in pools of light and the space between them is genuinely dark.
**Implies** radial key, grain shader or SVG turbulence, LUT via `feColorMatrix`,
controlled bloom. **Fails** when the grade crushes body copy below 4.5:1 and grain
eats small type. **Right when** the work is visual and benefits from being lit.

**Aurora / mesh gradient.** Large soft color fields drifting across each other with
no visible edges and no repeat. OKLCH interpolation keeps the midpoints saturated
instead of going gray, and motion is slow enough to be felt without being watched.
**Implies** OKLCH gradients, canvas or WebGL mesh, long-period animation, grain to
defeat banding. **Fails** as the default AI landing page, the most generated look of
the last three years. **Right when** it is a substrate for another style rather than
the style itself.

**Glow / neon.** A dark substrate with emissive accents that actually bloom, light
spilling past its source and tinting what it lands on. Edges glow from the inside,
shadows take the accent hue, two emissive colors at most. **Implies** layered
`box-shadow` bloom or a real bloom pass, dark tokens, hue-matched shadows.
**Fails** as halation that makes every string of text fringe. **Right when** the work
is nocturnal or technical and the emission points at the work.

**Vaporwave / Y2K.** Chromed type with environment reflection, cyan and magenta
gradient meshes, CRT scanlines and phosphor bleed, grids receding to a horizon,
deliberate JPEG and VHS artifacts. The nostalgia is specific to 1995–2003 hardware
and reads as costume unless committed to fully. **Implies** SVG chrome gradients, a
CRT shader, chromatic aberration, dithering, a period type pairing. **Fails** as
kitsch that dates the subject. **Right when** the audience shares the reference.

**Solarpunk.** Organic growth forms and botanical geometry under warm optimistic
light: curves derived from phyllotaxis rather than arbitrary blobs, terracotta and
sage and brass, layouts that branch rather than stack. **Implies** generative SVG
growth, warm gradients, curved layout paths, organic easing. **Fails** as generic
eco-branding with a leaf icon and a green button. **Right when** the work is climate,
agriculture, health, or civic.

## Motion-native

In these four the behavior **is** the aesthetic. A still screenshot cannot represent
them, which makes the `§12` reduced-motion design a first-class deliverable.

**Kinetic.** Nothing is at rest: type in perpetual motion, marquees running at
different rates by depth, letters responding to pointer velocity, composition
recomposing continuously. Stillness is used once, as punctuation. **Implies**
scroll-velocity input, variable-font axis animation, `requestAnimationFrame`,
transform-only compositing. **Fails** as exhausting, and unreadable when the thing in
motion is the thing being read. **Right when** the work is performance or sound.

**Physics-world.** Spring, inertia, mass, and collision are the interaction model.
Elements have weight, throwing them works, they settle rather than snap, and they
occupy space other elements respect. Nothing uses a duration; everything uses a
stiffness. **Implies** a physics loop, spring tokens instead of easing curves,
pointer velocity capture, a valid resting layout. **Fails** as a toy when the physics
never resolves into something readable. **Right when** the play makes a point.

**Scroll-cinema.** The page is a film reel scrubbed by the scrollbar: scroll position
maps to a timeline, sections pin while their contents advance, and the sequence has
shots, cuts, and cadence. **Implies** pinned containers, scrubbed timelines,
`will-change` discipline, preloaded frames, a real `§13` budget. **Fails** as
hijacked scroll that fights the user and strands anyone landing mid-page.
**Right when** the work has narrative order and one story to tell.

**Spatial / 3D-world.** The site is a navigable space with camera, depth, and
position. Sections are places, navigation is movement, and the sense of where you are
does the work a menu usually does. **Implies** WebGL or CSS 3D, a camera rig,
level-of-detail, a no-WebGL fallback per `§12`, an aggressive budget. **Fails** as a
maze where nobody finds the case study, which is `§7` violated structurally.
**Right when** a flat page would misrepresent the work.

## Technical and data

**Terminal.** Monospace throughout on a real fixed cell grid, blinking block cursor,
phosphor color on near-black, scanlines and slight CRT curvature at the edges.
Interaction is command-shaped and output persists in scrollback. **Implies** `ch`
units, a monospace with box-drawing coverage, a CRT shader, typed-output timing.
**Fails** as a gimmick with a fake prompt that accepts three commands and breaks on
the fourth. **Right when** the terminal is where the subject's work actually happens.

**Blueprint.** Drawing conventions applied literally: dimension lines with arrowheads
and measurements, section callouts, leader lines to annotations, hatching, a title
block, and a consistent line-weight hierarchy. Color is reserved for the ground.
**Implies** SVG line work, precise stroke tokens, annotation positioning, a drafting
typeface. **Fails** as decoration when the dimensions are fake and measure nothing.
**Right when** the callouts annotate actual work.

**Data-brutalist.** Dense tables, sparklines, and charts presented as the aesthetic
rather than as supporting evidence. Rules are hairlines, numbers are tabular,
alignment is decimal, and the interest comes from the density of true information.
**Implies** `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, real table semantics, inline SVG
charts. **Fails** the moment the numbers are decorative, which breaks `§5` outright.
**Right when** `EVIDENCE.md` can carry every number on the page.

**Wireframe / vector.** Line art only: no fills, hidden-line removal, contours and
edges describing volume through stroke alone, with weight variation carrying depth.
Objects read as constructed. **Implies** SVG or WebGL line rendering, hidden-line
computation, stroke-only tokens, draw-on animation. **Fails** as thin and cold at
sizes where strokes vanish. **Right when** the work is structural and the outline is
the honest view.

## Textural

**Risograph.** Two or three spot inks printed in separate passes with visible
misregistration, halftone dots in the shadows, and paper grain showing through.
Overprint areas produce a third color neither ink has alone. **Implies**
channel-separated layers, `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, per-channel offset, a halftone
shader, paper texture generated per `§10`. **Fails** as a filter when the
misregistration is uniform, since real registration error drifts. **Right when** the
subject is an illustrator, printer, or publisher.

**Xerox / degraded.** Photocopy artifacts as the medium: blown highlights, crushed
blacks, toner scatter at the edges, a slight skew, and generational loss where a copy
of a copy has lost its midtones. Contrast is brutal and midtones barely exist.
**Implies** threshold and dither passes, noise displacement, per-element skew, a
high-contrast duotone. **Fails** as illegible when applied to body copy rather than
to images and headers. **Right when** the work is zine, punk, or archival.

**Collage.** Layered scraps at mixed scale with torn edges, tape and staples, cast
shadows from real height differences, and elements rotated off axis. Scale jumps hard
between layers and the composition is assembled rather than laid out. **Implies**
irregular SVG masks, per-element shadow and rotation, generated paper and tape,
deliberate z-order. **Fails** as chaos with no reading order, losing `§6` immediately.
**Right when** the subject's practice is genuinely multidisciplinary.

**Ink / sumi.** Brush dynamics as the whole language: strokes with real pressure
variation, wet bleed into fiber, dry-brush breakup at speed, negative space treated
as the subject. One color, one gesture per composition. **Implies** SVG
variable-width paths, bleed via displacement, generated fiber, animation following
stroke order. **Fails** as a stock brush texture, which reads as clip art instantly.
**Right when** restraint is the position and the work rewards silence.

## Reductive

**Radical minimalism.** Type and space, nothing else: no borders, no cards, no
shadows, no illustration. Hierarchy comes only from size, weight, and distance, and
the whitespace is measured rather than left over. **Implies** one family with real
weights, a precise spatial scale, optical alignment, single-property motion.
**Fails** as empty and unmemorable when the copy is weak, since there is nothing else
to look at. **Right when** the writing is strong and the work needs no frame.

**Monochrome plus one accent.** A single hue's full tonal range carries structure,
and exactly one accent sampled from reality per `§8` appears only where attention
must go. The discipline is that the accent never decorates. **Implies** an OKLCH
lightness ramp, one accent token, usage rules stated in `DIRECTION.md`. **Fails** as
forgettable, the most common way a run looks competent and generic at once.
**Right when** it is the discipline layer under a louder collision partner.

**ASCII / text-only.** The page is characters: art drawn in a fixed cell grid, layout
built from box-drawing glyphs, images dithered into character density. Nothing is
rendered that could not be pasted into a text file. **Implies** monospace with full

underneath per `§12`. **Fails** as unreadable to screen readers and unusable below
400px. **Right when** the constraint is the point and the audience reads it as one.

---
